_doc: Weekly Instagram posting plan.
REWRITTEN 2026-08-13 (owner's rule, second pass). Every post carries THREE
sections, one slide each, seven rows each, every single day. The whole plan
is built around one question: what does this trip cost someone with a normal
LONG WEEKEND   2-4 nights, out Thursday or Friday and back Sunday or
Monday. Barely touches the working week.
WEEKISH        6-21 nights, LEAVING THURSDAY TO SATURDAY, returning any
day. A week that is allowed to bleed into a second and a
third. Merged from the old WEEK LONG and TWO WEEKS: split
in two, the long half could not fill seven rows without
padding (measured 2026-08-13, only nine destinations had a
two week trip at ANY price). Together they fill, and the
Thursday-to-Saturday departure is what keeps the section
honest about being weekend-shaped at the front.
CHEAPEST       the cheapest fares out of CLT at any shape. These are the
odd ones — a Wednesday to a Wednesday, days a 9-to-5 has to
actually book off. The slide says so rather than pretending
they are convenient. It makes NO discount claim, which is
why it can always fill and carry a thin day; a row still
wears the green badge if it genuinely cleared 12%.
NEVER AN OVERPAYMENT, ON ANY SLIDE. min_discount is 0.12 for the two trip
shape sections and 0.0 for CHEAPEST — zero, not negative. A cheap headline
price still above what that route normally costs is the SKIP row the owner
deleted in July, and it does not come back because a slide says 'cheapest'.
A section that cannot find seven shows fewer rows and prints the real count.
Never padded, never a lowered bar.
A city MAY appear in more than one section on the same day — a long weekend
in August and a fortnight in October are different trips. Never twice inside
one section, and the same exact flight never twice in one post.
`shapes` and `week` below are KEPT because pipeline/render_reel.py still
resolves a single daily shape for the reel. They do not drive the carousel.
`tag` is the short qualifier printed beside the cover on the slide. Keep it
comma-separated, never ' · ' separated: the header drops whole ' · ' segments
from the right when it would collide with the badge, so a tag containing ' · '
can half-survive and read as nonsense. Measured budget at MONO(26): roughly 40
characters for cover plus tag together. Over that and the slide counter goes
first, which is the intended sacrifice — the carousel dots already show it.

week.angle: A full week away, round trip, verified this morning.

weekend.angle: Out Thursday or Friday, back Sunday or Monday. A real long weekend, and you burn no vacation days.

urgent.angle: Long weekend shaped, leaving inside three weeks. Short window, real prices.

friday.angle: Expedia's 2026 Air Hacks Report puts Friday as the cheapest day of the week to book a flight, about 3% under Sunday, and the cheapest day to fly overall, up to 8% under a Sunday departure. Worth knowing: for US domestic routes specifically that report still has Tuesday as the cheapest day to actually fly, roughly 14% under Sunday.

twoweek.angle: The big one. Honeymoon, anniversary, the trip you keep putting off.

alternating._doc: Every other Sunday the two week post replaces the usual Sunday content. Twice a month max, on purpose, so it stays special. Parity is on the ISO week number.

_dow: 0=Mon 1=Tue 2=Wed 3=Thu 4=Fri 5=Sat 6=Sun. depart_dow/return_dow are the days a trip may leave and come back on; omit either to mean any day. LADDER: a shape matching nothing relaxes to nights-only, then to the wide window. Every board row records which rung it landed on (row['rung']).
